resolvedSinceRun01.evidence: Slither's arbitrary-send-erc20 detector does not fire anywhere in slither-firstparty-all.json at c91bc1a. story-001 replaced annihilateFrom(stable,from,recipient,amount) with annihilate(stable,recipient,amount); both halves now come from msg.sender and no allowance is consulted. The dual-asset allowance coupling that produced the run-01 High is structurally gone.
resolvedSinceRun01.caveat: This is a SAST negative, not a proof. Tier 2 should confirm no other path reintroduces third-party debiting.

resolvedSinceRun01.evidence: The strict-equality-against-zero guard was replaced by `if (mintedForStable != expectedForStable) revert PhUSDAmountMismatch(...)` against the minter's own calculateMintAmount quote (src/Antimatter.sol:234, 256). Slither's incorrect-equality detector no longer fires on first-party code. The run-01 residual question (under-mint, not zero-mint) is addressed by construction.

falsePositiveExplicitlyNotFired.explanation: The anticipated unchecked-return false positive did not materialise. Slither correctly recognises that both the success flag and the return data are checked on the very next line: `if (!ok || data.length != 32) revert DecimalsUnavailable(stable);`. unchecked-lowlevel appears nowhere in slither-firstparty-all.json. The staticcall surfaces only as low-level-calls (Informational) and missing-zero-check (Low), both normalised below with that context. Aderyn's unchecked-return detector likewise fired on 13 test-file sites and NOT on line 292.

findings.description: State written after an external call. setPhUSD reads minter.phUSD() then assigns phUSD (145-146); setPhUSDMinter reads newMinter.phUSD() then assigns phUSDMinter (158-159). Both are onlyOwner and the external callee is the owner-supplied minter/token.

findings.description: safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), stableAmount) at line 246 is followed by logic that assumes the full stableAmount arrived; a fee-on-transfer stablecoin would deliver less.
findings.note: PRESUMPTIVELY INVALID under the C4 known-invalid list (fee-on-transfer tokens are out of scope unless explicitly in scope) AND largely neutralised in code: the contract measures balances rather than assuming (stableBefore at 243, and the StableNotDeposited check at 254 reverts if the stablecoin does not fully leave). Passed through only so dedup/sanitizer disposes of it on the record rather than by silence.

findings.description: Raw low-level call: (ok, data) = stable.staticcall(abi.encodeCall(IERC20Metadata.decimals, ())) at line 292, used to cross-check the minter's registered decimals against the token's own.
findings.note: NOT an unchecked-return defect - the return IS checked (`if (!ok || data.length != 32) revert DecimalsUnavailable(stable);` at 293, then abi.decode and an equality check at 294-295). Slither's unchecked-lowlevel detector correctly did not fire. Surfaced at potential-low, above the usual low-level-calls discard, because this is the load-bearing new code in this regression range (Law 1: recall beats tidiness). The substantive Tier-2 question is not the call's safety but its CONSEQUENCE: toStableAmount now hard-requires every registered stablecoin to answer decimals() with exactly 32 bytes, so a token without decimals() - or one behind a proxy that reverts - makes annihilate() permanently unavailable for that stablecoin. The NatSpec acknowledges off-chain quote callers depend on this.

findings.description: The `stable` parameter is used as a call target at line 292 without a zero-address check.
findings.note: Benign by construction: address(0) has no code, so the staticcall returns ok=true with empty return data, data.length != 32 holds, and the function reverts DecimalsUnavailable(address(0)). It also cannot be reached with an unregistered stable because the yieldStrategy == address(0) check at 285 reverts StablecoinNotRegistered first. Test test_toStableAmountRevertsOnCodelessStable (test/Annihilation.t.sol:531) covers exactly this. Near-certain false positive; recorded for completeness.

findings.description: rescueERC20 sweeps an arbitrary token to an arbitrary recipient; the detector flags multi-address-token accounting breakage.
findings.note: The contract holds no accounted balances by design (NatSpec at 304-305: annihilate settles whole or not at all), so there is no accounting for a sweep to break. Overlaps SA-009 as owner surface. Likely QA at most.
